intro.heading: The instrument is the market. The contract count is your size inside that market.
intro.body: That distinction has to be crystal clear. MNQ, NQ, MGC, ES are instruments — they tell you what market you are trading. 1 contract, 2 contracts, 5 contracts tells you how much exposure you have to that instrument's move. Same market. Different emotional and dollar weight.
intro.dayliNote: Micros keep you teachable — smaller exposure gives you room to actually learn before your emotions hijack the lesson.

chart.heading: MNQ vs MGC — same 10-point move, different dollars
chart.prompt: Tap each instrument to see its per-point value.

left.label: MNQ
left.desc: MNQ moves $2 for every point. A 10-point move = $20.

right.label: MGC
right.desc: MGC moves $10 for every point — 5x MNQ's weight on the same 10-point move.

tapCards.prompt: MNQ moves $2/point, MGC moves $10/point. Both move 10 points in your favor while you hold 1 contract each. Which trade made more money?

options.label: The MGC trade — $10/point beats $2/point
options.feedback: Right — same move size, bigger per-point value, bigger dollar result.

options.label: They made the same amount
options.feedback: Same points moved, but very different dollar values per point.

tapCards.prompt: Now you take 5 contracts of MNQ instead of 1, same 10-point move. Did you switch instruments?

options.label: No — still MNQ, just more size and more dollar exposure
options.feedback: Exactly — the instrument didn't change, only your exposure to its movement did.

options.label: Yes — more contracts makes it a different instrument
options.feedback: Contract count changes size, not identity.

tapCards.prompt: A trader with a small account keeps taking 10 MNQ contracts on every setup because "it's just MNQ." What's the risk?

options.label: She's ignoring that size changes her dollar risk even with the same instrument
options.feedback: Right — "just MNQ" can still be a big risk if the size is large enough.

options.label: There's no risk — MNQ is a micro, so any size is safe
options.feedback: Being a micro contract doesn't make any size automatically safe.

quiz.question: A trader switches from trading 1 contract of MNQ to 5 contracts of MNQ. Has she changed instruments, and what actually changed about her trade?
options: No — she's still trading the same instrument (MNQ); only her size and dollar exposure changed
Yes — 5 contracts makes it a different instrument entirely
It's impossible to tell without knowing the price
quiz.explanation: The instrument stays MNQ — contract count only changes exposure.

quiz.question: Two traders both say they're "trading MNQ." One holds 1 contract, the other holds 20. Are they taking the same risk?
options: No — 20 contracts moves 20x the money on the same point move as 1 contract
Yes — same instrument means same risk
It depends only on which broker they use
quiz.explanation: Same instrument, very different dollar risk — contract count is what changes exposure.

quiz.question: Trading more contracts of the same instrument changes your:
quiz.explanation: More contracts means more dollars per point moved — not a different market.
